question: Which law of thermodynamics states that energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred or converted?
solution:
The correct answer is __**First Law of Thermodynamics**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **First Law of Thermodynamics** states that energy can neither be created nor destroyed; it can only be transformed from one form to another or transferred between systems.
 
• This law is also known as the **Law of Energy Conservation**.
 
• The mathematical expression of the First Law is: **ΔU = Q - W**, where ΔU is the change in internal energy, Q is the heat added to the system, and W is the work done by the system.
 
• It establishes the principle that the total energy of an isolated system remains constant over time.
 
• The First Law applies universally to all physical and chemical processes, from engines to biological systems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Zeroth Law of Thermodynamics**: Defines thermal equilibrium and forms the basis for the measurement of temperature.
 
• **Second Law of Thermodynamics**: States that the total entropy of an isolated system can never decrease over time and explains the concept of irreversibility in natural processes.
 
• **Third Law of Thermodynamics**: States that as the temperature of a system approaches absolute zero, the entropy of the system approaches a constant minimum.
 
• **Energy Transformation**: Common examples include the conversion of chemical energy to mechanical energy in engines or electrical energy to light energy in bulbs.
 
• **Applications**: The First Law is critical in understanding processes like heat engines, refrigerators, and biological metabolism.
